prerequisites: It is recommended to have successfully completed the subject "Materials Science and Engineering" from the second year, common to the Industrial Branch, to ensure basic knowledge of phase diagrams and alloy hardening mechanisms.

learning_outcomes.text: That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed those learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Applied knowledge of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Knowledge and skills for the application of materials engineering.

syllabus_topics: 5. Identification of Anodic and Cathodic Zones
Practical activity on the development of cements/mortars in collaboration with a foreign university (optional).
teaching_methods: Lectures (exposition in large groups of theoretical content and general applied examples)
Computer room practices in small groups
Debate of practical cases related to materials technology
Problem solving (problems and exercises proposed by the professor)

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and participation in proposed activities

assessment_rules: The final written exam must be passed with a grade greater than 5 out of 10. Attendance at practical sessions is mandatory. In the extraordinary call, it will be guaranteed that students can pass the subject, and if applicable, obtain the maximum grade, by taking an evaluation test.
